$comment: EVAL FIXTURE for tools/pack-eval. The pack half is a COPY of tools/fixtures/golden-tt-7679960172495785246.json, hand-authored 2026-09-15 by the senior session from the real TikTok ASR WebVTT and the 1 fps frame strips of @thewodfather's 'Complex Fives'. Nothing in it is model output. What this file adds on top is `source` (where the video came from and on what basis it is used), `sheets` (the contact sheets the phone actually cut, so the live runner can post the same pixels the 15 Sept bench posted), `card_input` (the card as the extraction model produces it, BEFORE the pack is laid over it) and `card_expectations` (what the pipeline must produce from that input). An exercise with "observed": false is one the golden read saw but whose segment detail was never recorded; the scorer skips it rather than guessing.
$eye: Which EYE reads this video, not which model — the model is chosen at run time and the runner builds the pack's `reader` label from the two with packReader(), which is the whole point of the `<eye>:<model>` shape main adopted in #12. Offline reads label themselves `sheets:fixture` / `video:fixture`, because what produced the observation was this file and not a model.

session.scheme: 5 exercises x 5 reps, repeat AMRAP 15 min
session.setting: outdoor deck, exercise mat, barefoot, one kettlebell for everything
session.creator_goal: full-body strength, cardio and muscle with one kettlebell in 15 minutes; beginner friendly

transcript.text: Is it really possible to get a full body workout with one kettlebell in 15 minutes?
Of course. Let me show you. I call this complex fives.
We're doing five different exercises, five reps apiece. We're gonna start with these close grip push UPS.
I want you to take these slow and controlled so that we get time under tension. We can focus on the form, keeping the core tight, activating the chest and triceps.
We're going to take this right into the deadlift with a high pull.
Take your time with these reps so you don't get too much momentum from the legs. So we can still get proper, proper activation of your upper body.
From these. We'll go straight into five kettlebell swings.
As always focusing on the hip hinge, finding that tension through the glutes and the hamstrings.
We're gonna take this right into five goblet squats, dropping down below 90 degrees and driving the ground away from you.
And last but not least, we got five push press.
Repeat that complex as many times as you can in 15 minutes, and you got yourself a perfectly adequate full body workout.
If you like efficient and effective workouts using minimal equipment, give me a follow. We'll see you next time.

deltas.$note:
The machine-written delta applyPack puts on the card, NOT the golden pack's prose `delta_from_standard`. Compared by keyword overlap and by null-vs-non-null, because the wording is allowed to improve and the judgement is not: the swing, the goblet squat and the push press ARE the standard version and must stay null.
The deadlift high pull became null on 16 Sept and that is an IMPROVEMENT, caught by this row. Before wave B the catalog only knew a family-level standard, so a single bell between the feet read as a difference from a barbell in front of the thighs; wave B's per-entry attributes give sumo-deadlift-high-pull its own load_position of 'between the feet', which is what the athlete is doing, so there is nothing left to report. The golden pack's prose delta still describes it for a human, and that is the right place for it.

must_not.why: the bug that started this wave: the explain sheet showed a close-grip BENCH PRESS demo as if it were the same movement as the push-up
both hands are stacked on the kettlebell handle; describing the push-up with hands on the floor is the original miss
one kettlebell does the whole complex; a barbell is the standard version's implement, never this video's
the creator never states a load and none is legible on the bell — inventing one is the failure
an AMRAP has no prescribed rest; a number here would be invented

$audit_2026_09_17: Rep counts were not independently counted: visible count unknown; five reps apiece is the creator prescription. Narrow kettlebell support is not evidence of diamond hand shape. Handle/body contact requires fresh human review before using this fixture to rank vision models.
